analysis.title: The Ghost of Winter of 2018 Will Bulls Suffer All the Way Until Christmas Eve
key_insights: The S&P 500 finished the week more than 4 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average. The last comparable extreme was August 25, 2015.
The one-week move in VIX this week was the fifth largest on record (per Bespoke).
The GS vol desk is drawing Q4 2018 comparisons, including an SPX overlay. VIX closed above 36 on Christmas Eve 2018, the day the S&P 500 hit its closing low.
Recent drawdown of hedge fund VIPs is among the worst on record (per Goldman).
US single stocks were collectively shorted every day this week. Weekly shorting activity was the largest since June 2022 and the third largest in the past decade (per GS Prime).
Hedge fund leverage has fallen from its 12-month highs by an amount in line with some of the most extreme episodes since 2018 (per JPM PI).
US nets and gross exposure are both at the zero percentile over 12 months (per Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage).
Gold had its biggest drawdown since the 1980s (per Morgan Stanley).
risk_factors: A repeat of the Q4 2018 path, in which the S&P 500 kept falling until its Christmas Eve closing low with VIX above 36.
Further forced de-leveraging by hedge funds, given the leverage decline and record weekly shorting.
